data.text/markdown:
Dissimilar edges and negative weights

In this notebook, we show how the number of repulsive edges and the magnitude of the negative weights can affect the embeddings, when creating embeddings based on weights. We use MNIST as a case study. The summary of what we'll find: the more dissimilar edges (and the larger the magnitude of the negative weight), the more uniformly spread out the embedding is. The fewer edges (and the smaller the magnitude of the weight), the more tightly clustered the embedding is. These comments are for when a standardization constraint is enforced. Without the constraint, the embedding can collapse to 0 if there are too few dissimilar edges. You should make sure to look at the MNIST notebook before going through this one.
Quadratic MDE problem
We start by computing a spectral initialization.
Dissimilar edges
First we vary the number of dissimilar edges, and show what effect this has on the embedding.

Negative weights

Next we vary the weights instead of the number of edges. The effect is similar to what happened when we varied the dissimilar edges.
